To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The use of a microprocessor in an instrument is not a guarantee that the instrument can be reprogrammed in the field; (2) The instrument can be reconfigured, but not reprogrammed, in the field; and (3) The use of the microprocessor as a memory device can increase the instrument’s flexibility, but at the cost of increased complexity and decreased reliability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a system for remote failure analysis of micro-based instrumentation.
the development of a microcomputer-based system for remote failure analysis of micro-based instrumentation.
the design of micro-based instrumentation for use in the field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the remote failure analysis of micro-based instrumentation has been successfully achieved.
, although the remote failure analysis of micro-based instrumentation is possible, it is difficult to achieve, especially in the case of a complex system.
there is no single, simple answer to the question posed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to develop a microprocessor based instrumentation package that can be remotely programmed, remotely reprogrammed and remotely tested.
we can now reprogram our instruments in the field.
the microprocessor is an excellent choice for many instrumentation systems, and that the design engineer need not be deterred from using the technology by the problems of remote failure analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the remote failure analysis of micro-based instrumentation is a powerful tool for the design engineer.
